::: {.callout-note .legacy appearance="simple"}
This post is from the blog I kept as Preceptor in Mathematics at Harvard (2005–2008). It's kept here as an archive; some links are dead and references are dated.
:::

When advising students on choosing their math courses, many are concerned about whether the [Math Xa](http://www.courses.fas.harvard.edu/1981){target="_blank"} and [Math Xb](http://www.courses.fas.harvard.edu/3857){target="_blank"} sequence will hurt their prospects of medical school admission. The [Harvard Office of Career Services](http://www.ocs.fas.harvard.edu) has a great site and a document called [Premedical Information for Harvard Students, Courses & Resources](http://www.ocs.fas.harvard.edu/careerresources/byfield/healthmedicine/coursereqs/2005premedguideshort.pdf). This guide says that the mathematics required for medical consists of one year, including **some** calculus. It also explicitly states that Math Xab is acceptable.

Math X is not a remedial course; it is an integrated precalculus + calculus course. It’s great for students who need the both. Students finishing Math Xb have proficiency at the level of [Math 1a](http://www.courses.fas.harvard.edu/8434){target="_blank"}. They can go on right into [Math 1b](http://www.courses.fas.harvard.edu/1804){target="_blank"} the following fall.
